question_en: You are invited to a Korean colleague's housewarming party. What is the most appropriate gift?
options: (A) A set of kitchen knives
(B) Laundry detergent or toilet paper
(C) A bottle of wine
(D) A bouquet of flowers

question_en: When receiving a business card from a Korean business partner, what is the most respectful way to handle it?
options: (A) Take it with one hand and put it in your pocket
(B) Receive it with both hands and read it carefully
(C) Place it on the table without looking
(D) Take a photo of it with your phone

question_en: In Korean culture, what does it mean when someone older pours you a drink at dinner?
options: (A) They want you to leave soon
(B) It is a sign of care and social bonding
(C) They are testing your alcohol tolerance
(D) It means they disagree with you

question_en: A Korean friend greets you by asking 'Have you eaten?' What does this most likely mean?
options: (A) They are inviting you to dinner
(B) They are literally asking because they are hungry
(C) It is a common greeting showing care for your wellbeing
(D) They think you look thin

question_en: Why might a Korean person avoid giving a gift with the number 4 prominently displayed?
options: (A) 4 sounds like the word for 'death' in Korean
(B) Even numbers are considered bad luck
(C) 4 represents dishonesty in Korean numerology
(D) There is no special meaning

question_en: At a Korean dinner table, a younger person is pouring soju for an elder. How should the younger person pour?
options: (A) With one hand casually
(B) With both hands or one hand supported by the other
(C) While looking the elder directly in the eye
(D) Into their own glass first as a taste test

question_en: In Korea, when is it common for couples to celebrate their relationship publicly?
options: (A) Only on wedding anniversaries
(B) On the 100th day anniversary and other numbered milestones
(C) Korean couples generally do not celebrate publicly
(D) Only on Valentine's Day

question_en: A Korean colleague says 'We should have a meal together sometime.' What does this typically mean?
options: (A) They are making a firm dinner reservation
(B) It is a polite social pleasantry, not necessarily a concrete plan
(C) They want to discuss a business deal
(D) They are asking you on a date

question_en: In Korean age culture, why do Koreans often ask someone's age when they first meet?
options: (A) To determine who should pay for the meal
(B) To establish the appropriate level of speech formality
(C) It is considered rude and should be avoided
(D) To decide seating arrangements only

question_en: What is the significance of 'red ink' when writing someone's name in Korea?
options: (A) It signifies celebration and good luck
(B) It is associated with death and should be avoided for living people
(C) It means you are angry at the person
(D) It has no special cultural significance

question_en: In Korea, what does 'nunchi' refer to?
options: (A) A traditional Korean board game
(B) The ability to read the atmosphere and others' feelings
(C) A type of Korean tea ceremony
(D) A formal greeting between strangers

question_en: When a Korean person turns away or covers their mouth while drinking alcohol with elders, this is because:
options: (A) They don't like the taste of the drink
(B) It is a sign of respect to not drink facing the elder directly
(C) They are trying to hide how much they are drinking
(D) It is a superstition to avoid bad luck

question_en: In Korea, what is the cultural attitude toward eating alone in a restaurant?
options: (A) It is completely normal and very common
(B) It has traditionally carried a social stigma, though this is changing
(C) It is considered a sign of wealth and independence
(D) Restaurants will refuse to serve a single diner

question_en: Why do many Korean buildings skip the 4th floor in elevator numbering?
options: (A) It is a structural engineering requirement
(B) Because 4 is associated with death, so floors jump from 3 to 5 or use 'F'
(C) The 4th floor is always reserved for storage
(D) This practice does not actually exist

question_en: In Korean gift-giving culture, what should you do when someone offers you a gift?
options: (A) Open it immediately to show enthusiasm
(B) Refuse it at least once or twice before accepting
(C) Accept it and set it aside without opening
(D) Ask how much it cost

question_en: When greeting an older Korean person formally, what is the standard gesture?
options: (A) A casual wave
(B) A bow, deeper for higher status or seniority
(C) A kiss on both cheeks
(D) Snapping fingers

question_en: Upon entering a Korean home, what is expected?
options: (A) Keep your shoes on at all times
(B) Remove your shoes at the entrance and step onto the raised floor
(C) Remove only your right shoe
(D) Shoes are optional in modern Korean homes

question_en: At a Korean meal, why does almost every dining table include kimchi?
options: (A) Kimchi is rare and reserved for special occasions
(B) Kimchi is a national staple banchan served with nearly every meal
(C) Kimchi is only eaten by elders
(D) Modern Korean cuisine has phased it out

question_en: At a Korean meal, you should NEVER stick your chopsticks upright in a bowl of rice because:
options: (A) It can cause spills
(B) It resembles incense offered to the dead at ancestral rites — considered very inauspicious
(C) It is considered a sign of wealth
(D) There is no such taboo

question_en: What is a 'jjimjilbang' in Korean culture?
options: (A) A type of street food
(B) A public bathhouse / spa with hot tubs, saunas, and communal sleeping areas
(C) A traditional school
(D) A Buddhist temple

question_en: What is 'Seollal' in Korean tradition?
options: (A) Korean Independence Day
(B) Lunar New Year — families gather, perform sebae bowing, eat tteokguk
(C) A summer harvest festival
(D) A modern shopping holiday

question_en: What is 'Chuseok' in Korean culture?
options: (A) A K-pop awards show
(B) Mid-autumn harvest holiday — ancestral rites, family gathering, songpyeon rice cakes
(C) A national mourning day
(D) Korean Valentine's Day

question_en: When is hanbok typically worn in modern Korea?
options: (A) As everyday clothing
(B) On major holidays (Seollal, Chuseok), weddings, and special ceremonies
(C) Only by performers on TV
(D) Never; it is illegal to wear in public

question_en: Until late 2022, why might a Korean person say they are '2 years older' than their international age?
options: (A) Korean people are biologically older
(B) Traditional Korean age counts age 1 at birth and +1 every Lunar New Year (now phased out by law)
(C) It is a joke that never had basis
(D) Tax brackets in Korea differ

question_en: In Korean numerology, the number 7 is generally considered:
options: (A) Unlucky and avoided
(B) Lucky, often associated with good fortune
(C) Associated with funerals
(D) A neutral number with no significance

question_en: At a traditional Korean funeral, what is the traditional mourning color?
options: (A) Red
(B) White hemp clothing was traditional; modern funerals now also use black
(C) Bright yellow
(D) Green

question_en: When older relatives offer you food at a Korean gathering, the polite response is often:
options: (A) Refuse firmly and never accept
(B) A gentle initial refusal or acceptance, then receiving food respectfully (often with both hands)
(C) Eat immediately without acknowledgment
(D) Demand more food

question_en: Why does the depth of a Korean bow vary in different situations?
options: (A) It is purely random
(B) Depth signals respect — deeper bows for elders, formal apologies, or higher status
(C) It only varies by neighborhood
(D) Bow depth is not culturally significant

question_en: What is 'hoesik' (회식) in Korean workplace culture?
options: (A) A morning prayer at work
(B) Company dinner/drinking events that build team bonding; historically near-mandatory
(C) A type of office software
(D) A retirement ceremony

question_en: What is 'Suneung' (수능) and why is it a national event?
options: (A) A traditional dance
(B) College entrance exam — country pauses (flights delayed, traffic limited) to support test-takers
(C) A holiday for retirees
(D) A summer music festival

question_en: Why do Koreans use sibling-like titles ('oppa', 'hyung', 'unni', 'noona') even with non-relatives?
options: (A) Everyone in Korea is actually related
(B) Age-based honorifics extend to friends/seniors — reflects Confucian respect for seniority
(C) These words have no relational meaning
(D) Only K-pop fans use them

question_en: What does 'Hangul Day' (October 9) commemorate?
options: (A) The first Korean president's birthday
(B) The promulgation of the Hangul writing system by King Sejong
(C) Liberation from Japanese rule
(D) National sports day

question_en: In Korea, same-sex friends (especially women) sometimes hold hands or link arms in public. This is:
options: (A) A sign of romantic relationship
(B) Common platonic affection between close friends
(C) Strictly forbidden
(D) Only seen in elderly people

question_en: On Korean public transit (especially subways), the cultural norm is to:
options: (A) Speak loudly to entertain other passengers
(B) Keep voices quiet and avoid phone calls; reserved seats are strictly for elderly/pregnant
(C) Eat full meals
(D) Play music aloud

question_en: Why do Koreans often use 'uri' (우리, 'our') instead of 'my' — e.g. 'uri eomma' (our mom) instead of 'my mom'?
options: (A) The Korean language lacks a word for 'my'
(B) Collective identity is culturally emphasized; 'uri' signals shared belonging
(C) It is grammatically required only in writing
(D) The custom is not actually practiced

question_en: What is 'chaemyeon' (체면) in Korean social life?
options: (A) A traditional dance
(B) Saving face — preserving social dignity and reputation, important in interactions
(C) A Korean dessert
(D) A type of friendship contract

question_en: When pouring soju for an elder, what is correct etiquette?
options: (A) One hand casually
(B) Use both hands (or support pouring arm with the other), bottle's label facing up
(C) Pour with eyes closed
(D) Spill some on the floor first

question_en: In a Korean PC bang ('PC방'), what activity is most associated with the space?
options: (A) Religious services
(B) Multiplayer online gaming (e.g. League of Legends, StarCraft); high-end PCs, hourly fees
(C) Government tax filing
(D) Karaoke singing

question_en: Why do Korean cafés often serve as study spaces for students?
options: (A) Cafés legally must allow studying
(B) Long study sessions over coffee are widely tolerated; quiet, Wi-Fi-equipped cafés are abundant
(C) Studying in cafés is forbidden
(D) Korean students never study in cafés

question_en: What is the Korean superstition of 'fan death'?
options: (A) A modern wellness practice with scientific backing
(B) Folk belief that running an electric fan in a closed room overnight can be fatal — not supported by science but persistent
(C) A historical regulation
(D) A K-drama plot device only

question_en: In Korean popular culture, blood type is often used to:
options: (A) Determine eligibility for surgery only
(B) Stereotype personality traits (A=careful, B=passionate, etc.) — informal but widespread belief
(C) Assign government IDs
(D) Choose university majors

question_en: What is the global cultural impact of K-pop?
options: (A) Limited to Korea only
(B) Major export industry — global fanbases, tours, K-pop language learning, tourism
(C) Banned outside Asia
(D) A short-lived 2000s trend

question_en: What is 'Yeondeunghoe' (Lotus Lantern Festival)?
options: (A) A modern light-art exhibit
(B) Annual Buddhist festival around Buddha's Birthday, with lantern parades; UNESCO Intangible Heritage
(C) A nationwide power outage event
(D) A summer fireworks event

question_en: At a Korean meal, what are 'banchan'?
options: (A) The main dish only
(B) Side dishes (often many small plates) served with rice — kimchi, namul, jeon, etc.
(C) Dessert plates
(D) Beverages

question_en: In Korean drinking culture, what is generally avoided?
options: (A) Toasting in general
(B) Pouring your own drink — others should pour for you (and vice versa)
(C) Saying 'cheers'
(D) Drinking from a glass

question_en: What does 'aigoo' (아이고) express in Korean?
options: (A) A greeting only
(B) An interjection expressing fatigue, sympathy, surprise, or mild frustration (multi-purpose 'oh dear')
(C) A formal apology
(D) A goodbye

question_en: What is 'jeong' (정) in Korean interpersonal culture?
options: (A) A type of currency
(B) Deep emotional bond / attachment built over time between people — often considered uniquely Korean
(C) An official government title
(D) A type of formal address

question_en: Why is delivering food at midnight common in Korean cities?
options: (A) Restaurants legally must operate 24/7
(B) Robust late-night delivery culture, especially for chicken/jjajangmyeon — feeds late-night socializing
(C) Daytime delivery is illegal
(D) Korean cities lack restaurants

question_en: At a Korean coffee shop, what does it usually mean if a young person sits alone with textbooks and a laptop for hours?
options: (A) They are not allowed to study
(B) Studying solo in cafés ('cafe-gongbu') is a widely accepted norm
(C) They are visiting from abroad
(D) Café staff will ask them to leave

question_en: In Korean military service culture, what is broadly true for South Korean men?
options: (A) Military service is illegal
(B) Conscription requires most able-bodied men to serve roughly 18-21 months
(C) Service is purely voluntary
(D) Only women serve in Korea
